answer: Sequential Effort Ledger. Each identity must anchor itself to a unique slice of a shared physical timeline: an operator solves a chained puzzle whose solution time is fixed by hardware speed, and the chain forces new identities to start after prior completions. A ledge in the ledger caps parallel slots per operator facility, verified by power draw signatures. Each identity then proves its chain position through a prism of timing attestations. Faking N identities costs N sequential wall-clock intervals, so growth is linear in real time, not in capital.
